observation_summary: The system fails to return the correct primitive type (e.g., returning an Integer instead of a Double) when providing default values for primitive types, leading to ClassCastExceptions and assertion failures.
reasoning_summary: The failure occurs because the logic responsible for returning default values for primitives is incorrectly mapping or handling the primitive type conversion. This is a procedural error in the method responsible for determining the default return value, which is a classic Algorithm/Method defect. It is not a missing guard (Checking) or a simple initialization error (Assignment/Initialization), but rather an incorrect implementation of the logic that maps types to their default values.
evidence_used: java.lang.ClassCastException: class java.lang.Integer cannot be cast to class java.lang.Double
evidence_gaps: Production code snippets were not provided, requiring inference from test failures and stack traces.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not just an incorrect constant value, but a failure in the logic that determines which value to return based on the requested type.
While it involves type handling, the core issue is the internal logic of the default value provider, not a mismatch in the interface contract between two components.
